newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turk Cypriot leader postpones talks with Hannay.
newsitem.headline: Turk Cypriot leader postpones talks with Hannay.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash on Monday postponed talks with Britain's envoy on the Cyprus dispute, David Hannay, in protest at what he said was unequal treatment of the island's two communities.

"Treating the Greek Cypriots as the official government and treating us as a community cannot be reconciled with the principle of equality," Denktash told reporters in announcing the postponment of the meeting.
Hannay started an intensive round of contacts on the divided island on Monday ahead of U.N.-sponsored settlement talks on the decades-old conflict next month.
He held an hour-long meeting with Cyprus President Glafcos Clerides and was later expected to cross to the north of the island for talks with Denktash.

The Turk Cypriot leader called off the talks after hearing reports that Hannay was also meeting the Greek Cypriot foreign minister and speaker of parliament, while he was only to meet with Denktash in the north.
He told reporters he would discuss the matter at a lunch meeting with Hannay set for Tuesday.

Turkish forces invaded northern Cyprus in 1974 after a brief Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military then ruling Greece. Some 30,000 mainland Turkish soldiers are stationed in northern Cyprus, declared a breakaway state in 1983 but recognised only by Ankara.

Denktash and Clerides are to meet in New York on July 9, their first meeting in three years, to try to end the 23-year division of Cyprus. Last week U.S. President Bill Clinton appointed Richard Holbrooke, negotiator of the 1995 Bosnia peace accord, as special emissary for Cyprus.

"What we were focussing on was how it should be possible for this negotiation process, when it starts, to bring what I call an early harvest, some progress to illustrate the credibility of the process but also to start to move things forward," said Hannay after meeting Clerides.
The British diplomat, who arrived in Cyprus on Sunday, qualified earlier statements about the existence of common ground in the positions of the two sides, saying he preferred the word convergence.
